title: Your First Python Program
summary: Learn how to write and run your first Python program using print()
learningObjectives: Understand what Python is and why it's popular
Learn to use the print() function

sections.content:
Welcome to Python! Python is one of the most popular programming languages in the world. It's known for its simplicity and readability, making it perfect for beginners.

Python is used everywhere - from web development to data science, AI, automation, and more. The best part? It's free and open-source!
Let's write your first Python program. In Python, we use the print() function to display text on the screen.
Python uses indentation (spaces) to define code blocks. Unlike other languages that use braces {}, Python uses 4 spaces or a tab.
Python is case-sensitive! 'Print' and 'print' are different. Always use lowercase 'print' for the print function.
Many beginners forget to include quotes around text. Remember: print("Hello") not print(Hello). The quotes tell Python it's a string of text.
Now let's try something more interesting. We can print multiple things and even do math!
Try this example that prints different types of data:
sections.codeExample:
print("My name is Alice")
print("I am 25 years old")
print("I like programming")
sections.expectedOutput:
My name is Alice
I am 25 years old
I like programming

keyTakeaways: Python uses print() to display output
Text must be enclosed in quotes
